0 Ubongo Each player receives one set of 12 tiles. At the beginning of each round, each player also receives a new puzzle board. The task to be completed on each puzzle board is determined by rolling the die; immediately afterward, the hourglass is turned over. All players simultaneously try to place a predetermined set of tiles on the light-colored placement area of their puzzle boards in such a way that the area is completely covered. Each player who can complete their task before the hourglass runs out shouts “Ubongo!” and takes a gem from the bag — the two fastest players also receive a bonus gem from the game round track. You win if, after 9 rounds, you have the most valuable gem collection. Number of players: 1 - 4 Game duration: 7 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Ubongo and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Damn you spacial reasoning skills!!!  I am horrible at games like this.  They frustrate me, more than relax me.

[Rating: 2/10] A game? No, more a puzzle solving exercise, against the clock. Not my sort of thing.

[Rating: 2/10] (Scott) If you can make a game out of this, you can make a game out of anything.  Only saving graces are brevity and consistent nastiness.

[Rating: 2/10] Really, really don't like it. I get why some people like it, but to me it's just an "extremely annoying game" which I "won't play ever again". Played this a couple of times, too.

[Rating: 2/10] Tetris element is cute - but scoring is seriously whacked and having to play grabbing match against other players is just horrible. I hated that sort of game in kindergarden and I still hate it now

[Rating: 2/10] I'm not terribly good at spacial-perception, pattern-recognition type games, and when you add a clock to put pressure on me, it drains all of the tiny amount of fun potential.

[Rating: 2/10] This game induces stress of the frantic kind. A timer. A mad rush to fit a bunch of patterns together. Some like it. I don't.

[Rating: 2/10] I feel ashamed to have this game in my collection. I feel shame to ask anyone to trade it. That's what happens when people that have no idea about board games try to buy you a secret present. This is not a board game. This is a Tetris Clone Puzzle that someone forced into it 2 or 3 "rules" and components to call it a board game. Managed to play one whole game. After 5-6 years in the closet I recently found a way to use it. I have my 2 and 4 year old daughters roll the dice and based on the roll win diamonds. They have 100xtimes the fun I had playing it.

[Rating: 2/10] No. Just no.  And never again.  As a puzzle by myself, maybe. Probably not, though.  As a race against other players, no way.  In case there's any doubt: no. No, thank you.  (My aversion to this game is such that it has become a running joke at my local game club!)
